Month given as Pauṣa (?) with the uncertainty of reading 'paṣṭa' kept in notes
Notes: VS 1857 and ŚS 1722 agree (both 1800 CE); Pauṣa śukla 8 of VS 1857 probably falls in late Dec 1800 or Jan 1801

date.as_written: śamvat 1857 śāla paṣṭa śudi 8 roja 7 śāke 1722

notes: The scribe is not named ('liṣītam edam postakam'). VS 1857 (−57) and Śaka 1722 (+78) both give 1800 CE, so the two eras agree. 'paṣṭa' is probably a corrupt spelling of Pauṣa, though this is not certain. If it is Pauṣa śukla 8 of VS 1857, the date falls around late December 1800 or January 1801. 'śāla' (year) and 'roja' (day) are Persian-derived words; 'roja 7' means the seventh weekday, Saturday. Ascribing the Ghaṭakarpara poem to Kālidāsa is a traditional attribution; it is often credited to a poet named Ghaṭakarpara instead. The śloka after the colophon (dvijarājamukhī…) is a stray verse and names no persons.
